draft.title: Other ways government intervenes
card: Welfare payments
money paid to people who need support, such as the unemployed or people with a disability, to help them meet basic needs.
Regulations
rules that businesses must follow, such as safety standards for products, to protect consumers and workers.
Subsidies
payments to businesses that lower their costs, so they can charge less or produce more of a good that benefits the community.
Competition laws
laws that stop businesses from joining together to fix prices or misusing their market power, so consumers keep fair choices.
draft.remember: Each tool is a way government fixes a problem the market leaves or protects consumers.

a.q: Which tool is a rule that businesses must follow to protect consumers?
a.why: A regulation is a rule businesses must follow, such as a product safety standard. A subsidy is a payment to a business, and a welfare payment goes to people who need support.
a.clue: Which tool is a rule, not a payment?

b.q: Three bakeries in a town agree to all charge the same high price for bread. Which tool is designed to stop this?
b.why: Competition laws stop businesses from agreeing to fix prices, so consumers keep fair choices. Product safety regulations are also rules, but they deal with safe products, not price agreements.
b.clue: The problem is businesses working together on price.

problems.detail: Competition laws are also rules businesses must follow to protect consumers; the card calls them 'laws that stop businesses…', so 'A competition law' is defensible too. The stem needs a distinguishing detail, such as safety standards for products.
Why (a) explains why the subsidy and welfare payment are wrong but never says why a competition law is not a rule businesses must follow to protect consumers. That leaves the ambiguity unresolved.

a.q: The government says every child car seat must pass a crash test before it can be sold. Which tool is this?
a.why: A crash test rule is a safety standard for a product, which is a regulation. A competition law is also a law, but it stops price fixing and misuse of market power, not unsafe products. A subsidy and a welfare payment are payments, not rules.
a.clue: Is this rule about prices and rivals, or about the product itself?
